req_server_lead: The PC that holds the band's songs and stays on. An older PC is fine.
req_cpu_rec: 4 cores or more, with AVX2 (Intel 4th gen, AMD Ryzen or newer)

req_gpu_rec: Not needed: heavy processing runs overnight

req_storage_lead: 28JoursBox itself adds little: about 45 MB per analyzed song for the separated tracks (measured: 154 songs = 6.9 GB). What fills the disk is your own files: rehearsal WAVs and Cubase / Studio One projects. Edited and deleted files are also kept 30 days (versions and trash).
req_ex1: 100 songs in MP3 / m4a (about 5 MB each)
req_ex2: 100 rehearsals in WAV, 4 min (about 40 MB each)
req_ex3: 20 multitrack Cubase / Studio One projects (1 to 5 GB each)
req_ex_note: Tracks are separated automatically overnight for m4a files, and on request for WAV and MP3. Plan an external disk of the same size as your data for backups.
req_time_text: Each new song is prepared overnight (1 am to 7 am): beats, chords, separated tracks and fine analysis. Measured on an 8-core PC: about 2.6 minutes of processing per minute of music, so about 10 minutes for a 4-minute song and around 30 songs per night. On a 4-core PC, count about twice as long. New songs are ready the next morning; a large first import can take a few nights. Heavy processing is capped (at most 3 cores for analysis, 6 for separation, one song at a time) so the server stays responsive.
req_members_text: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. About 320 MB for the software, plus the space of the folders you choose to keep on this PC. Cubase or Studio One optional: project locks are set automatically if they're installed.
req_phones_text: iPhone or Android with a recent browser (Safari, Chrome). Nothing to install, no storage used: songs play from the server. On mobile data, listening uses about 0.2 to 0.3 Mbit/s.
req_office_min: Optional: LibreOffice (free) on the server PC
req_office_rec: Install it in its default folder: it is detected automatically. Without it, everything else works but Office files can't be previewed.
faq_office_q: Can I view Word, Excel and PowerPoint files?
faq_office_a: Yes, on phones and in the browser, provided LibreOffice (free) is installed on the server PC, in its default folder. The server converts each document to PDF the first time it is opened, then prepares new ones at night. Without LibreOffice, the app shows "Preview unavailable" for these files; everything else works.

hero_eyebrow_dc: The bands' answer to data centers
home_desc_dc: Your songs, rehearsals and projects on your band's own PC, not in a data center: private sync for every PC and phone, separated instruments, chords, tempo, loops. Free, no subscription.
dc_home_title: Your music has no business in a data center
dc_home_lead: Online storage services keep your rehearsals and unreleased demos in distant buildings owned by large companies, and charge you every month for the space. 28JoursBox does the opposite: everything stays on a PC in your band.
dc_c1_p: Files, versions, takes, analyses, separated tracks: everything is on the disk of your server PC. No third-party service stores your songs.
dc_c2_p: No price per member or per gigabyte. You buy a disk once and pay the electricity of a PC. Our band: about 720 GB on a 4 TB disk.
dc_c3_p: Instrument separation, chords, song structure and even speech-to-text transcription are computed on your PC, not by an online AI provider. Your demos and meetings never leave.
dc_c4_p: No company account, no terms that change overnight, no price increase. Your files are ordinary files on each PC, readable without 28JoursBox.
dc_home_more: Why not the cloud? Read the full argument →
faq_dc_q: Why not just use an online storage service?
faq_dc_a: Because your songs would then live in a company's data center, under its terms and its prices, which grow with every gigabyte and every member. With 28JoursBox, they stay on your band's PC, the AI runs there too, and there is nothing to pay per month. The full argument.
faq_backup_q: What if the server PC breaks down?
faq_backup_a: Every member's PC keeps a full copy of the folders it syncs, so your files are not lost. But the server's history, trash and analyses are only on its disk: that's the flip side of independence. Make a regular backup to an external disk, ideally kept somewhere else. The user guide explains how.
dl_dc_note: Your server PC becomes your band's own data center, at home. No space to rent, no subscription. In return, you're in charge of its backup: plan an external disk.
don_dc_p: Your donation keeps 28JoursBox free and independent: an alternative to data centers that belongs to the bands who use it, not to a company that rents them storage.
why_title: Why not the cloud? 28JoursBox vs data centers
why_desc: Why 28JoursBox keeps your band's music on your own PC instead of a data center: data ownership, costs, local AI, energy, and the honest flip side.
why_h1:
Your songs have no business
in a data center.
why_lead: 28JoursBox is our answer: a private cloud and a rehearsal studio that run on a PC in your band, at home. Here's why, and what it changes, including what it asks of you.
why_s1_t: Where do your files go today?
why_s1_p1: When a band shares its rehearsals through an online storage service, every WAV, every Cubase project, every unreleased demo is copied into a data center: a huge building full of servers, owned by a large company, often in another country.
why_s1_p2: The same goes for AI practice apps: to separate the instruments or find the chords, your song is sent to their servers. You pay for the space every month, per account, and the price follows the gigabytes. The rules (prices, quotas, terms of use) are set by someone else and can change at any time.
why_r1_b: On your server PC's disk, at home
why_r2_a: At the provider, under its rules
why_r3_a: Your song is uploaded to an AI provider
why_r3_b: Computed at night on your PC
why_r4_b: From your PC: straight from your router with direct access, or through an encrypted tunnel (Tailscale) that relays the traffic without storing your files
why_r5_b: Through the email account your admin chooses
why_r6_a: Every month, per account, per GB
why_s3_p: With an online service, the bill grows with the volume and the number of members, and comes back every month. With 28JoursBox, it's a one-off purchase and the electricity of a PC. Here are realistic orders of magnitude, not promises.
why_k2_l: our band's real files, on that same disk
why_k3_l: electricity of a PC on 24/7 at 30 W (about 260 kWh)
why_k4_l: per member, per gigabyte, per month
why_s3_note: Electricity estimated at €0.20–0.25 per kWh. A mini-PC that draws 10 W costs about €20 a year. If the PC is already on for other uses, the extra cost is almost zero.
why_s4_t: Taking back control of your data
why_s4_l1: No account at a company. The band is its own host: one pseudonym per member, one group password, and the admin is one of you.
why_s4_l2: Your files stay ordinary files. Each member's PC has a normal folder, readable and usable without 28JoursBox. Uninstall it: your files stay.
why_s4_l3: Your rules. You decide how long versions and trash are kept, who joins, and who is removed. No terms of use that change overnight.
why_s4_l4: Unreleased stays unreleased. Your demos and the AI analyses of your songs never leave your PC. Public links are created only when you decide.
why_s5_p1: According to the International Energy Agency, data centers used about 415 TWh of electricity in 2024, around 1.5 % of the world's consumption, and this should double by 2030 (about 945 TWh), driven largely by AI. A single typical data center uses as much electricity as 100,000 households.
why_s5_p2: 28JoursBox doesn't claim zero impact: a PC at home uses electricity too. But it replaces distant, duplicated, always-on servers with a single PC that your band controls, often one that already exists. Heavy processing runs at night, one song at a time, at low priority. And a 4-minute song is analyzed once, not every time someone opens it.
why_s5_src: Source: IEA, Energy and AI (2025).
why_tips_l1: Reuse a PC you already have, or a low-power mini-PC.
why_tips_l2: Put the songs on a dedicated disk, not on an SSD bought just for this.
why_tips_l3: Keep separated tracks only for the songs you actually work on: they weigh about 45 MB per song.
why_s6_p: Bringing your data home also means taking on what a provider used to do for you. We'd rather say it clearly.
why_s6_l1: Backups are your responsibility. Copy the server's data regularly to an external disk, ideally kept in another place. The user guide shows how.
why_s6_l2: The server PC must stay on. If it breaks down, members keep their local copies, but sync and the phone app wait until it's back.
why_s6_l3: Security is shared. Keep the group password within the band, change it if the link leaks, keep Windows up to date. From outside, access goes either directly to your router (a port you open, protected by HTTPS) or through an encrypted tunnel (Tailscale), a third-party service that relays traffic but stores none of your files. Updates for members' PCs are signed, and each PC checks it is really talking to your band's server.
why_cta_p: Install 28JoursBox on a PC in your band tonight: your files, your server, your rules.
rec_title:
Record the rehearsal on your phone.
Rework the song the next day.
rec_lead: No sound engineer, no cables, no computer in the rehearsal room: one phone is enough to make quick demos. Then everyone, at home, can suggest a structure and make their own version of the song, which the others can hear.
rec_s1_p: + › Record audio, then the big red button, on a real drum groove (100 reference grooves in 10 styles, recorded in a studio) or a simple click. When you stop, the played part is pre-selected, the level is set, and the take is already cut into patterns: tap one to loop it. Trim and fade with a finger.
rec_s2_t: No network? Keep it on the phone
rec_s2_p: Rehearsal rooms rarely have Wi-Fi: choose Keep on the phone, then Send all once you're back on the network. The take travels lossless (FLAC, about twice as light as WAV), resumes by itself after a cut without losing anything, and lands as an m4a in the folder you chose.
rec_s3_p: As soon as it arrives, your band's server analyzes it by itself: tempo, bars, sections, A/B/C patterns, chords. At night it also separates the vocals, guitars, bass and drums. On your PC, not in a data center.
rec_s4_p: In the advanced player, the song arrives already cut into colored sections. Then it's up to you:
rec_s4_l1: move sections and blocks: long press, then drag;
rec_s4_l2: change their order, duplicate, delete, keep only a selection;
rec_s4_l3: name the sections: Intro, Verse, Chorus, Bridge, Solo…;
rec_s4_l4: repeat a loop as many times as you want (×2, ×3, ×8…), even a drum loop of a few seconds, with no gap;
rec_s4_l5: extract a selection as a new file, or save the whole new arrangement.
rec_s4_note: Everything can be undone. Corrections to the sections are shared with the whole band.
rec_s5_p: Still in the advanced player, the red button records a take over the song, aligned to the music. It becomes a mixer track and a file shared with the band, ready for Studio One or Cubase.

rec_s6_p: Save your arrangement: it becomes a new file in the band folder, which the others can listen to and comment on. When the structure is settled, To Studio One or Cubase creates a ready-to-open project with separated tracks, or you take the WAV into any DAW.
